'''''Dasylirion longissimum''''', common name the '''Mexican grass tree''', is a [[species]] of flowering plant native to the [[Chihuahuan Desert]] and other [[Deserts and xeric shrublands|xeric habitats]] in Northeastern Mexico.<ref>Lem., Ill. Hort. 3(Misc.): 91 (1856).</ref>

==Description==
Evergreen trunk-forming shrub, slow and moderate growing to {{convert|4|to|6|ft}} tall and wide, and can be up to {{convert|12|ft|m}} tall by {{convert|8|ft|m}} in diameter. The long bladed leaves are up to {{convert|4|ft|m}} long by {{convert|0.24|in|mm|0}} across.<ref name=":0">[http://www.monrovia.com/plant-catalog/plants/815/mexican-grass-tree.php Monrovia; ''Dasylirion longissimum'']</ref>

==Cultivation==
{{unreferenced section|date=June 2023}}
This drought-tolerant and dramatic ''Dasylirion'' is cultivated by nurseries for use in both personal gardens as well as public or corporate [[xeriscaping|xeric]] landscapes, mainly in the [[Southwestern United States]] (from [[Texas]] west to [[California]]). It is valued for its soft and billowing, ''Agave''-like form, which the plant has in its early life, resembling a thin- and multi-leaved agave plant. As it matures, the plant will grow a small stalk or trunk at the base with the foliage growing out of the top. ''D. longissimum'' is naturally hardy to {{convert|15|°F|°C|abbr=on}}.<ref name=":0" />
